_readme: Reconciliation map for the 2026-11 bulk import of cargrid_cars.json (3812 records). Decisions recorded in docs/IMPORT-REVIEW.md. 'excludeTheirs' drops an incoming row because our catalog already holds that exact car under a different id (decision D12: our id wins). 'renumberTheirs' and 'renumberOurs' apply decision D13: whichever generation number is accurate wins, neither file by default.

excludeTheirs.pontiac-firebird-trans-am-g2: = our pontiac-firebird-g2; their model string is 'Firebird / Trans Am'
excludeTheirs.pontiac-gto-g4: = our pontiac-gto-g5, which is renumbered to g4 below
excludeTheirs.land-rover-defender-g2: = our land-rover-defender-g3, which is renumbered to g2 below
excludeTheirs.dodge-dart-g1: 1960-1976 catch-all spanning four real generations and overlapping our dodge-dart-g4 (1967-1976). A single row cannot be four generations; dropped rather than imported.
excludeTheirs.chevrolet-chevelle-g1: 1964-1967 = our chevrolet-malibu-g1, which is the top Chevelle trim of those years. Leaves Chevelle at g2/g3 with no g1, which CLAUDE.md permits.
excludeTheirs.ford-f-series-g2: 1953-1956 = our ford-f-250-g1 and ford-f-350-g1, the same trucks at different weight ratings

pontiac-gto-g5.why: GTO has four generations: 1964-67, 1968-72, 1973-74, 2004-06. Ours was off by one.

land-rover-defender-g3.why: The Defender nameplate runs 1983/1990-2016 then 2020-. Ours counted the Series I-III era, which was not badged Defender.

dodge-dart-g2.why: Dart generations: 1960-61, 1962, 1963-66, 1967-76 (our g4), 2013-16. The revival is the fifth, not the second.

subaru-wrx-g5.why: Numbering is scoped to the nameplate per CLAUDE.md. 'WRX' as its own nameplate starts 2014/15 (our g1), so the 2021 car is g2. The earlier cars are a different nameplate, 'Impreza WRX STI', imported with its own g1-g3.

subaru-wrx-sti-g4.why: Same nameplate-scoping rule: 'WRX STI' standalone begins in 2014.

deferUntilUnfolded._note: These incoming rows are variants of a record we currently hold folded, so importing them now would count the same engine twice. Each is held back until its parent is shrunk in the same operation -- which needs the parent's base figures sourced, and needs the variant's own image. Only two of the eleven candidates the detector flagged are genuine; the rest (Pagani Huayra Roadster, Mercedes EQS SUV, Ford Mustang Mach-E, Phantom Drophead Coupe, Charger Daytona, and four Pajero rows) are separate cars that a model-name prefix test mistook for variants.
deferUntilUnfolded.dodge-challenger-srt-demon-g3: 2018 Demon, 808-840 hp. Our dodge-challenger-g3 reads 250-1025, where 1025 is the 2023 Demon 170. The nameplate needs splitting as a unit: base/R-T/SRT8 parent, plus SRT Hellcat, Hellcat Redeye, SRT Demon and Demon 170 records. Sources conflict on the mid-range figures (Scat Pack quoted at both 470 and 485), so this needs a sourced pass, not a guess. Note the shrink will drop the 1000+ bucket below the floor of 8 until the Demon 170 record exists -- correct, since that bucket was partly propped up by a record claiming 1025 hp for a plain Challenger.
deferUntilUnfolded.hyundai-elantra-n-g1: 276-286 hp. Our hyundai-elantra-g7 reads 139-276, where 276 is exactly the N. Shrink the parent to the non-N line-up in the same operation that imports this row.

keepBoth._note: Fuzzy matching flagged these as possible duplicates. They are not: each pair is a parent and a separately-recorded variant or body sibling, which decision D11 keeps apart.
